Current code: both pass. Independent scratch script with own stub pool: mixed [bad, 1, bad, 2, 3] wrote [1,2,3], task alive, join returned, 2 error logs (one per bad alert) both with traceback; bad alert alone: nothing written, alive, join returned, 1 error log with traceback.

DATABASE_URL on closed port: exit 3, logs "app.db: database unavailable ... ConnectionRefusedError" and "app.main: startup failed: Postgres is unreachable or DATABASE_URL is empty/wrong ...", "Application startup failed. Exiting." Fake ws log empty (no upstream connection). No URL/password in log.
Empty DATABASE_URL + RULES_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=true: exit 3, same startup failed line, no ws connection.

Valid PG: started, health 200, rule POST 201, one upstream subscribe, alerts persisted. PG stopped (immediate) while running: health 200, GET/POST rules and GET alerts 503, "rule fired" count kept rising (8 -> 12 in 4 s) so ticks still processed, no crash (asyncpg pool background tracebacks logged only). PG restarted: within ~6 s /api/rules, /api/alerts 200 and POST rule 201 (endpoints DO recover). Alerts fired during the outage were dropped (accepted limitation): 40 fired vs 21 stored in that run.

Pre-created watchlist table without created_at plus one alert_rules row: exit 3, db error UndefinedColumnError then startup failed; no ws connection. (Without any alert_rules row the backfill has nothing to insert and startup succeeds, as expected.)

Compose YAML parses (PyYAML). postgres healthcheck CMD-SHELL pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-ticks}, matching the service's own defaults; backend depends_on postgres condition service_healthy; frontend depends_on unchanged ([backend]). git diff HEAD on the file: +8/-1, only those two blocks. docker compose was NOT run (docker not installed).

Scratch: 10000 enqueue_alert calls on a full queue (size 1) took 0.081 s, queue size stayed 1, exactly 1 warning ("alert queue full; dropped 1 alert(s) since last warning"); after advancing time.monotonic by 11 s, next drop produced one warning "dropped 9999 alert(s)". Drop-point comment present in _write_alert_rows (Intentionally dropped, not requeued).

CLAUDE.md fail-loud text, flag meaning, healthcheck, invariant 5, Alert writer paragraph match the code. Known issues: writer-dies and startup-not-fail-loud removed; accepted-limitation item (now 4) kept; renumbered 1-6 consistent. Minor imprecisions (not blocking): (i) opt-out says endpoints answer 503, which holds only when no usable DB (with flag false and a valid DATABASE_URL, Database.connect still connects and endpoints work); (ii) startup-failed log line says "unreachable or DATABASE_URL is empty/wrong" even when the real cause is a schema/backfill failure (the preceding app.db line gives the exception type); (iii) app.db message says "persistence disabled" though startup then aborts; (iv) backoff sentence says sleep only if a row failed, it also sleeps after an unexpected writer error.
Real server, clean DB: one rule POST -> exactly 1 upstream subscribe, 6 "rule fired" lines and 6 rows in alerts, GET /api/alerts returns them.

No python processes of mine remain (fake ws, uvicorn, pytest all stopped); my PG cluster stopped and temp dir removed. The 7 postgres.exe Services-session processes are the same pre-existing PIDs as before I started. git log -1 = 68afb62. git status lists the same 21 entries as the initial snapshot (conftest.py, test_api_symbols.py, docker-compose.yml were already modified in it). No git state-changing command was run.
